findings.rationale: Only direct specs validate override keys. Business and requirements branches merely replace matching VerifyItems, so misspelled or inapplicable --instances/--values entries are silently ignored and the sweep runs with unintended bounds.

The early return occurs before VerifyBounds are inspected. A spec with no entity/number declarations can therefore contain bounds for undeclared names; those bounds survive lowering and are later ignored instead of rejected.

Neither named domain declarations nor general Range types check lo <= hi. Such types enumerate no values while default_value still manufactures lo, causing inconsistent state domains and potentially vacuous verification.

Unlike actions, properties have no name registry, and terminal has no duplicate check. Duplicate invariants/transitions/reachables/leadsTo targets become ambiguous, synthesized Until names can collide with explicit declarations, and a second terminal silently replaces the first.

Struct fields are resolved and stored without checking field-name uniqueness. Later consumers represent struct values with BTreeMap, so duplicate declarations collapse to one entry and the declared TypeDef disagrees with runtime values.

Zero divisors are checked, but i64::MIN divided or remaindered by -1 also overflows and Rust's div_euclid/rem_euclid panic. A user-supplied constant expression can therefore abort model construction instead of returning ModelError.

with_origin unconditionally replaces an existing precise diagnostic origin, even when the replacement is None, while at records only ModelError.span and Display never consults that field. Nested type-expression errors can consequently lose their exact location or render with no location at all.
